newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Saudi spent $1.1 trillion on development in 25 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Saudi spent $1.1 trillion on development in 25 yrs.

text.p: Saudi Arabia has spent 4.2 trillion riyals ($1.12 trillion) on development projects over the past 25 years, Planning Minister Abdul-Wahab bin Abdul-Salam Attar said in remarks published on Sunday.
Attar's remarks, published in the English-language Arab News, did not include a breakdown or details of the projects.
The daily also said that Saudi Arabia, the world's largest exporter and producer of oil, had increased its non-oil exports by 70 percent from 1985 to 1994.

Quoting a statistical report, it said Saudi Arabia exported 365.15 million tonnes of industrial and agricultural products worth 159.59 billion riyals in 1994, up from 126.8 million tonnes worth 92.35 billion riyals in 1985.
It imported goods worth 87.42 billion riyals in 1994, slightly up from 85.56 billion riyals in 1985, the paper said.
"The value of the kingdom's imports remained stable except in 1990 and 1991 when the imports slightly (rose)," it said, quoting the report.
